title: 2021 Fall AMC 10A Problem 17
statement: An architect is building a structure that will place vertical pillars at the vertices of regular hexagon \(ABCDEF,\) which is lying horizontally on the ground. The six pillars will hold up a flat solar panel that will not be parallel to the ground. The heights of pillars at \(A,\) \(B,\) and \(C\) are \(12,\) \(9,\) and \(10\) meters, respectively. What is the height, in meters, of the pillar at \(E?\)

solutions.text:
Put a regular hexagon in coordinates with \(A=(-1,0),\) \(B=(-\frac{1}{2},\frac{\sqrt3}{2}),\) \(C=(\frac{1}{2},\frac{\sqrt3}{2}),\) and \(E=(\frac{1}{2},-\frac{\sqrt3}{2}).\) Because the solar panel is flat, the height is an affine function \(h(x,y)=ux+vy+w.\)

From \(h(A)=12,\) \(h(B)=9,\) and \(h(C)=10,\) subtracting the last two equations gives \(u=1.\) Then \(-u+w=12,\) so \(w=13.\) Using \(h(B)=9\) gives \(-\frac{1}{2}+\frac{\sqrt3}{2}v+13=9,\) so \(\sqrt3v=-7.\)

Therefore \[ \begin{aligned} h(E) &=\frac{1}{2}-\frac{\sqrt3}{2}v+13 \\ &=\frac{1}{2}+\frac{7}{2}+13 \\ &=17. \end{aligned} \]

Thus, D is the correct answer.
hints: A flat panel means height is linear over the ground plane
Use regular-hexagon coordinates and a function \(ux+vy+w\)
